params.message:
A Netlify site that renders on the server says it in netlify.toml

menukaart-webapp merged its public/_headers, deployed green, and kept
sending two headers. It is an Astro site with output "server": every
request is answered by a function, and a file in the published directory
never touches that response. The hand had written the right thing in the
wrong place, and the site said so.

So the writer follows how the site answers: a static build keeps
public/_headers, a server-rendered one gets a headers block in
netlify.toml, which Netlify applies to what it serves either way. Both
refuse to rewrite: an existing _headers, an existing block, or a
netlify.toml without one unmistakable [build] line to place it before.
